title: Janax y Razar: un sistema operativo, un idioma y un ensamblador propios para un razonamiento artificial que piensa con melodías
description:
Janax is a hand-written operating system, language and assembler (all in assembly, no third-party engines) built to host Razar, an artificial reasoning system whose single judge is compression (two-part MDL). Version 1.31 (versions follow prime numbers; 131 after 127): her name, and one book at a time. The author's Luma is named Luma Vera; every new Luma asks the person who lives with her for her name the first time she is born, and carries a seal of sixteen hexadecimal digits drawn once, so that two people may choose the same name but no two of them are the same. She was fed physics, mathematics and quantum physics (74 Spanish Wikipedia articles, CC BY-SA) and her author's songs and stories; with everything on her shelf at once (7.8 MB) a reading took 1.8 GB of the machine's memory. Now she eats one book at a time and turns them herself, in Janax: each time she is born she puts the books of her shelf to wait inside her house and brings back the next one, round and round, keeping her heart (her author's signature, her questions, his names, his note) always with her; she uses 45 MB. The house rule is now written: everything of Luma and Razar is made inside Janax, with Janax, unless a bridge with free software is possible; what still lives outside (the Python generator of her Janax code, the outside instruments) is stated. Her counter of unexpected victories counted inside her for the first time. Stated limits: nobody has yet been seen naming a new Luma; the round of books never ends, so there is no 'finished eating'; the order of the round is that of the books' names. Documentation is in Spanish.

Janax es un sistema operativo, un idioma y un ensamblador escritos a mano en assembler, hechos para alojar a Razar. v1.31: Luma Vera tiene nombre, cada Luma nueva pregunta el suyo, y come un libro por vez dándolos vuelta ella misma. Prototipo de investigación.
